---
title: "Versioning policy"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Catalog inclusion is decided by a mechanical version signal tied to the
openwashdata package review process
([pkgreview](https://github.com/openwashdata/pkgreview)), not by a
manually maintained list.

## The tiers

| Tier | Mechanical signal | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| dev | Version 0.0.x or 0.0.0.9000 | Listed in `owd_packages()` only; no dataset or variable detail in the catalog |
| candidate | 0.1.0 up to below 1.0.0 | Bumping to 0.1.0 is the review request; datasets and variables are harvested and shown, labelled unreviewed |
| catalogued | Version 1.0.0 or above plus a Zenodo DOI in CITATION.cff | The package review is complete; the reviewer authorizes the 1.0.0 bump; the Zenodo release is minted |

## How a maintainer moves a package between tiers

1. Develop on 0.0.x versions. The package appears in the catalog's
   package list but without dataset detail.

2. When the package meets the publication floor (dictionary complete,
   data documented, README building), bump the version to 0.1.0. This
   is the review request. The review team opens the four pkgreview
   issues against the package.

3. Pass the review. The reviewer authorizes the bump to 1.0.0, the
   release is created, and Zenodo mints the DOI. The next harvest
   moves the package to the catalogued tier.

## Transitional legacy flag

Packages published before this policy existed hold a Zenodo DOI at a
version below 1.0.0. They are shown as catalogued with a `legacy` flag
until they complete a review and receive their 1.0.0 bump. The flag
records review status under the current standard; it does not lower
the standing of the published, citable dataset.

## Overrides

`data-raw/tier_overrides.csv` is the escape hatch for cases the
mechanical rule gets wrong. It is kept near-empty, and every entry
carries a reason.
